note: Claims about the installed command surface, verified by scripts/scan-command-surface.mjs. Every hostOnly entry carries an anchor that must still appear in the command file, and every verb claim names a handler symbol that must still exist at the cited path. Nothing here is prose a reader has to trust: if a claim rots, tests/command-surface.test.mjs fails.

classes.A: The CLI verb performs the work. The host renders its JSON and derives no state. Gaps listed under cliGaps must be closed in the CLI, with tests, before the command is thinned.
classes.B: The command owns orchestration no verb performs. The CLI takes the derivable state; the host keeps the named capabilities. Thinning to a renderer would delete them.
classes.C: No legion verb exists. Placement is undecided; see P16-B009.
classes.cliGaps: Every gap carries a disposition: build-in-cli (the CLI gains it before the command is thinned), keep-in-host (it is inherently host work), or deliberate-removal (it does not survive, and why). A gap with no disposition is a capability assigned to nobody, which is how a conversion passes every criterion while the behaviour disappears.

commands.rationale: The verb is deterministic and executor-free, and an earlier revision read that as equivalent. It is not. Both are called the codebase map and they are different artifacts: renderCodebaseMarkdown emits a file-extension histogram over records of {path, sha256, sizeBytes, lineCount, symbols, headings, summary}, where symbols come from seven regexes. The command emits an architecture document with a dependency graph, an API surface, a coverage map, and ranked risk hotspots, produced by executing skills/codebase-mapper/SKILL.md. They do not share a path either: the command writes .planning/CODEBASE.md and refreshCodebaseMap writes a run-scoped .legion/project/workflow/map/<run>/codebase.md. Thinning would replace the architecture document with the histogram, which is the deletion the contract says is indistinguishable from the intended outcome. The CLI owns the derivable state: the file set, the fingerprint, freshness, scope containment, and the run record.

hostOnly.capability: The analytical half of the map: architecture narrative, dependency and import graph, route and API surface, data and config map, test and coverage map, risk hotspots, and the package map
Ranked risk hotspots in the completion report
Semantic search over the verb's ranked matches: classify the query into keyword, path, symbol and domain hints, say why each matched, and name the source files to read next

cliGaps.gap: A bare legion map is now a read-only summary; --refresh is required for the destructive path.
Freshness now has four states: fresh, stale, partial (the stored map covers a different scope) and absent.
The 30-day age rule is implemented against the map's generatedAt.
An empty source set now refuses with map_no_source and writes nothing.

legion map --query refuses --scope rather than silently ignoring it. The query runs over the stored map, whose scope was fixed when it was generated, so accepting the flag would answer from the whole repository under the caller's chosen path.

legion map --check and --query no longer write guidance runs. Recording a read evicted the refresh that produced the map from the twenty-run window getLatestCodebaseMap scans, so reads destroyed the ability to find what they read.

commands.rationale: Deterministic, but not equivalent. handleMilestoneWorkflow reads exactly one file, its own milestones.json, and never reads a roadmap, phase, or requirement artifact. --define stores the free-text --phases string opaquely without cross-referencing it. --complete checks only that the id exists and stamps the operator's own --summary. --archive sets a status field and moves nothing. No git commit and no gh invocation exists anywhere in packages/cli/src, so the completion commit and the GitHub milestone close have no counterpart at all.

hostOnly.capability: Cluster roadmap phases into proposed milestone groupings by theme and dependency, then negotiate the grouping with the operator
Interactive action loop offering only the actions the current milestone state permits
Routing a menu selection to the matching mode
Commit the milestone completion in the project's conventional format
hostOnly.anchor: Create git commit following execution-tracker Section 6 milestone completion format

hostOnly.capability: Close the corresponding GitHub milestone when gh and a remote are available
Per-milestone deep dive naming which requirements the milestone satisfies
hostOnly.anchor: Requirement coverage: which requirements are satisfied by this milestone

cliGaps.gap: --complete refuses a milestone that is already completed or archived, and refuses while any phase in its parsed range is incomplete, naming each one. The command's stated no-partial-completions rule is the verb's.

--archive flips status to archived and sets archivedAt. The command moves phase directories from .planning/phases/ to .planning/archive/milestone-N/; both paths retire, so the relocation is a recorded deliberate removal rather than an open gap. An equivalent over .legion artifacts would be new work, not preservation.

Status mode is read-only. It used to fall through to the same write path as define, complete and archive — rewriting milestones.json, regenerating milestones.md, and appending a guidance run on every invocation — so a host that renders status on every display filled the run history with records of someone looking.

Progress is rendered by joining a milestone's parsed phase range to the changes behind those phases: completed of covered, a bar, and a per-phase table naming each change and why an incomplete phase is incomplete. A range that does not parse reports unresolvable with the parse error rather than zero progress.
--summary is stored verbatim, so a completed milestone's summary is whatever the caller typed rather than derived from the artifacts the CLI owns.

Summary generation is unowned. The command gathers plan, requirement, file, agent, outcome and decision data to compose a completion summary; the verb stores the caller's free-text --summary verbatim. Neither the CLI requirement nor the host-retained list claimed it, so conversion could replace computed milestone evidence with an operator-typed string and satisfy every criterion.

The archive confirmation goes with the relocation. Its text reports how many phase directories will move and where, so retaining it after the relocation is removed would ask the operator to approve an operation that no longer happens. If a confirmation survives it is a new one about the status transition, not this one.

commands.rationale: The verb is executor-backed and purpose-built, and an earlier revision stopped there. Follow --phase through the handler: it reaches slugSource, runInput, and an interpolated topic string handed to guidancePrompt, and nothing else. It is never parsed as a phase number and never selects any evidence. Worse than scope being ignored: guidancePrompt receives only the workflow, the topic, and four section names, so the executor producing the findings sees no project evidence at all. resolveWorkflowState().stage and the last two guidance runs are read before the run but consumed only by renderGuidanceMarkdown after it. A scoped retrospective over completed work is not a mode this verb has, it is a word pasted into a prompt.

hostOnly.capability: Save-or-discard decision, including a view-only path that persists nothing
Section-by-section correction of the findings before they are recorded
Cross-project aggregation across every project in the portfolio

cliGaps.gap: --phase N and --milestone M are both real selectors. --phase resolves through the derived chg_phase-<N>- ID; --milestone resolves its parsed phase range to that set of changes. Both gate on completeness and narrow evidence gathering to their changes, and project-wide stage and recent runs are excluded under any scope.

The executor now receives the project's committed evidence: stage, change count, task count, passing reviews and recent runs, rendered into the prompt rather than only into the markdown written afterwards.

Evidence gathering from completed-work artifacts (phase summaries, review findings and cycle counts, plan frontmatter) does not exist. latestGuidanceRuns returns run metadata, not build or review evidence.

A scoped retro refuses a phase whose change is not complete, using isChangeComplete (taskgraph non-empty, every task's latest evidence accepted, an accepted review present). An unscoped retro reports over current state and is not gated.

Counts over typed artifacts are gathered and put in front of the executor: changes and how many are complete, tasks, passing reviews, escalations with their reasons, and the first-pass review rate. Under --phase they cover that change alone.
--dry-run reports the gathered evidence and writes nothing, decided before the run directory is created.
Findings reach a read surface: retro appends every finding to .legion/project/workflow/retro/retro-index.json, following the knowledge-index.json convention. Staged writing remains open separately.

No staged-write path. runRetroWorkflow writes retro.md and the guidance run before it returns, so the host's view-only choice still persists and edit-before-saving edits findings already recorded. The retained save/discard and edit choices are impossible at this boundary until the CLI gains a non-persisting run followed by an explicit save.

The retro-to-plan loop is closed at both ends. legion plan reads the retro index and reports outstanding major and blocking actions in its payload and human output, including on --dry-run. Plan runs no executor, so it surfaces the actions to the caller decomposing the phase rather than acting on them.

commands.rationale: The verb implements one of the command's four modes, and implements it without the type system the other three are built on. LessonIndex records carry {id, lesson, createdAt, artifactPath} and nothing else, so pattern, pitfall, and preference do not exist in the CLI's data model. There is no read path: the only consumer dumps the whole index into a context pack truncated at 4,000 characters with no query. Recall, list, and prune have no verb surface at all.

hostOnly.capability: Classify the lesson as pattern, pitfall, or preference and confirm the classification before recording
Enrich the lesson with derived tags, a one-line summary, and the current phase context
Multi-turn recording session that loops back for the next lesson after each save

cliGaps.gap: Lesson records carry a typed kind, tags, and a summary, so --list can group and --recall can score a tag match 3 and a summary match 2.

--recall searches lessons and retrospective findings, and reports corpus: ["lessons", "retrospectives"]. Findings score on title and body only; they carry no tags, and a synthetic tag would rank them above lessons for a reason the caller cannot see.
--list groups recorded learning by kind and reports the unclassified count.
--prune targets .planning/memory/OUTCOMES.md, which does not survive. No outcome record store exists in the CLI; record as a deliberate removal.

Prune mode is removed rather than built, and is removed from the argument hint, usage text and mode routing along with its step so nothing advertises a route the host cannot execute. It archived OUTCOMES.md records older than memory.prune_threshold. That setting does still exist in settings.json and docs/settings.schema.json; what does not exist is OUTCOMES.md, any archive path, or a verb that removes entries from the lesson index.

commands.rationale: Proposed as class A on the grounds that the command dispatches no agent and its writes all target .planning/ files. A skeptic refuted it and was right: the command scores every check PASS, WARN, or FAIL, and the verb has no severity concept. ArtifactDiagnostic and TraceabilityDiagnostic carry only code, message, and source, and validateProject fails as soon as any diagnostic exists. Thinning today would turn every warning into a hard failure, which is a behaviour change for anyone running validate in CI.

hostOnly.capability: Repair-then-reverify loop that re-runs validation over the fixed files and presents an updated result set
hostOnly.anchor: Then re-run validation on fixed files and show updated results.

hostOnly.capability: Per-check fixability policy: decline to auto-fix anything whose correct value is a decision, and never edit a requirement to make its hash match
hostOnly.anchor: Do NOT auto-fix anything whose correct value is a decision.

cliGaps.gap: WARN severity exists: ArtifactDiagnostic carries an optional severity where absent means error, only blocking diagnostics decide ok, and warnings are reported through the existing warnings channel with status valid_with_warnings. var_not_ignored is the first demotion, and doctor's two shallow path checks are now reported rather than computed and dropped.
--ci is a recorded deliberate removal and is now refused rather than silently accepted. --json already carries the full typed payload; the three-valued exit code has no counterpart.

The root settings.json is validated by an executable Zod mirror in @legion/core, read through packages/cli/src/workflow/settings-check.ts and reported by both legion validate and legion doctor. A mirror rather than the published schema because there is no JSON Schema validator in the tree and docs/settings.schema.json is checksum-frozen; a parity test holds the two in agreement. Absence is a reported state, invalid values are warnings, and only unparseable JSON fails.

--fix is a recorded deliberate removal and is now refused rather than silently accepted: every fix target is a .planning/ file that retires, and parseCliArgs used to swallow the flag so it appeared to work.
The agent-roster check compares against strings in STATE.md and .planning/config/authority-matrix.yaml. Both retire, so the check has nothing left to compare. Deliberate removal.

The .planning/config/control-modes.yaml half of the command's step 9 does not survive: the file retires with the directory, and docs/settings.schema.json carries the control_mode description that referenced it.

The dangling-agent-reference half of the fixability policy retires with the .planning/ agent catalog it guarded. The policy itself survives, restated against the case that outlives it: requirement-set drift must never be silenced by editing the requirement.

commands/validate.md advertised --fix and --ci in its argument-hint while the CLI refuses both. The hint is removed; the removals were already recorded and the command now says so in its authority section.

commands.rationale: The verb runs one executor pass against fixed sections and writes one artifact. The command runs a divergent design conversation: an entry-path choice, a bounded research pass, an iterative clarifying interview over eight named decisions, and an approach-comparison loop. Rendering the verb's payload would delete all of it. Exploration is the one place the governing plan deliberately grants wide latitude, so this is the command least safe to thin.
